messages.content: I need to narrow down flights for an Atlanta district review. The review is Monday at 2:30 p.m. in Buckhead, and Tuesday I have a restaurant visit in Sandy Springs from 9:00 to about 11:30. Compare going Sunday evening with Monday morning, then an early or evening return Tuesday. Don't book anything yet.
What dates are you traveling, and which Chicago airport should I use?
October 18 through 20, 2026. Use O'Hare. Nonstops only for this one.

I found two useful outbound nonstops. Sunday, October 18, the flight leaves ORD at 6:35 p.m. and reaches ATL at 9:31 p.m. Monday, October 19, the morning option leaves at 7:05 a.m. and arrives at 10:02 a.m. The Sunday flight gives you a settled start but requires another hotel night. The Monday flight leaves roughly four and a half hours before the review.
How much real margin does the Monday flight leave once I get out of the airport and up to Buckhead?

Allow about 35 to 50 minutes to exit after arrival if you have no checked bag, then 30 to 50 minutes by car to Buckhead in late-morning traffic. That puts you at the review location around 11:10 a.m. to 11:45 a.m., leaving approximately 2 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours 20 minutes before 2:30. MARTA to Buckhead would be more predictable at about 45 minutes from the airport station, plus walking time.
That's enough. Now check Tuesday. I cannot assume the site visit ends early.

The early nonstop departs ATL at 1:50 p.m. and arrives ORD at 2:59 p.m. The evening nonstop leaves at 6:10 p.m. and lands at 7:22 p.m. From Sandy Springs, the airport drive is commonly 35 to 55 minutes outside the worst traffic, but an accident can extend it.
Spell out the early-flight timing if I leave the restaurant at 11:30.

Leaving at 11:30 a.m. would put you at ATL around 12:05 to 12:25 under ordinary conditions. That leaves 1 hour 25 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes before departure. It is workable with carry-on luggage and prompt departure from the site, but a visit running 20 minutes late or a traffic delay would make it uncomfortable. The 6:10 p.m. flight leaves more than four hours of cushion even if the visit runs long.
What are the round-trip totals for each sensible pairing? Economy is fine, and include the Sunday option even though it adds the room night.

The current round-trip totals are $318 for Monday 7:05 a.m. outbound with Tuesday 1:50 p.m. return, $344 for Monday 7:05 a.m. outbound with Tuesday 6:10 p.m. return, $382 for Sunday 6:35 p.m. outbound with Tuesday 1:50 p.m. return, and $409 for Sunday 6:35 p.m. outbound with Tuesday 6:10 p.m. return. These are standard economy totals before any optional seat or bag charges.
The $344 combination looks right. Is there any operational reason to pay another $65 and go Sunday?

Only if you want to remove Monday-morning flight disruption from the critical path. The Monday arrival has a reasonable traffic margin for the 2:30 p.m. Buckhead review, so Sunday is not necessary based on the published schedule. Sunday would also add one hotel night and a late airport-to-hotel transfer, likely 25 to 40 minutes by car to Buckhead at that hour.

Use Monday at 7:05 and Tuesday at 6:10 as the working flights. Carry those times, the meeting locations, transfer estimates, and the $344 airfare into the hotel and transportation comparison. Do not purchase them.

Set for research only: Monday, October 19, ORD-ATL nonstop departing 7:05 a.m. and arriving 10:02 a.m.; Tuesday, October 20, ATL-ORD nonstop departing 6:10 p.m. and arriving 7:22 p.m.; current round-trip airfare $344 in standard economy. The Monday review is at 2:30 p.m. in Buckhead, with an estimated 30 to 50 minute airport drive and arrival near the venue around 11:10 to 11:45. The Tuesday Sandy Springs visit runs from 9:00 to about 11:30 a.m.; the airport drive is estimated at 35 to 55 minutes, and the evening flight provides ample margin. I will use the Sunday 6:35-9:31 p.m. outbound, the Tuesday 1:50-2:59 p.m. return, and their timing and cost tradeoffs as comparison points when evaluating hotels and ground transportation. Nothing has been purchased.
